examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Draw overlapping regions only to establish membership, then count algebraically. Distinguish |A|, the number of subsets, and the number of elements of a power set. Inclusion–exclusion alternates signs: single-set counts overcount pairwise overlaps, while subtracting all pairs removes a triple-overlap three times and requires adding it back once.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
In a universe of 100 elements, |A|=50, |B|=45, |C|=40; pairwise intersections are 20,15,10 and the triple intersection is 5. How many elements lie in none of the sets?

**Answer: 5.** The union has 50+45+40−20−15−10+5=95 elements. Its complement has 100−95=5. Pairwise intersection counts include the triple intersection.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
State the universe before using a complement. ‘Only A’ excludes all intersections; |A| itself includes them.

The empty set is a subset of every set, but need not be an element of every set.
